clips.title: How to write a JQL query in Jira | Jira Software tutorial
clips.why: Atlassian's own short tour of JQL in the search box: the same text our poll sends to the API.
look: A query is built from a field, an operator and a value, joined with AND or OR.
The finding-unassigned-issues example searches on the assignee field, the field our poll searches on too.
Notice that the result is a list you can sort: we sort by updated so the oldest change comes first.
clips.after: Nova's poll runs project = RH AND assignee = currentUser() AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY updated ASC, as the Nova service account.

clips.title: API Pagination: Making Billions of Products Scrolling Possible
clips.why: A clear picture of the two ways APIs hand out pages, and why a cursor beats an offset when the data keeps changing.
look: Offset pagination: you ask for "skip 100, take 100", and items can move between pages while you read.
Cursor pagination: the server gives you a bookmark, and you send it back for the next page.
clips.after: Jira's nextPageToken is a cursor. Tickets change all the time, which is exactly the case the video describes.

clips.title: Webhooks vs API Polling
clips.why: The honest trade-off between asking for changes on a timer and being called when something happens.
look: Polling costs requests even when nothing changed, which is why rate limits matter to a poll.
A webhook needs a URL on the internet that the other side can call.
clips.after: We accept the cost of polling every minute so that nothing on the internet can call our platform; the workflow ID makes the repeats harmless.

practice.q: Complete Nova's JQL so the poll finds open RH tickets assigned to the caller, oldest change first.
practice.after: AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY updated ASC
practice.hint: A JQL function that means "whoever is calling".
practice.why: The poll calls Jira as the Nova service account, so currentUser() means Nova, and the query never needs Nova's accountId written in it.

practice.q: RH-1239's changelog has one assignee change to Nova, made by Omer, and Dana commented "@Nova go" an hour later. Who is the requester?

options.why: He made the only change that set the assignee to Nova. A comment does not hand a ticket over.
Her comment is text anyone could type. The changelog, written by Jira, decides.

options.text: Nobody, because there are two people
options.why: Only assignee changes to Nova count, and there is exactly one.

practice.q: Put one run of the poll in order.
items: POST the JQL search and get the first page
Send the search again with nextPageToken until no token comes back
For each ticket, read the property, then the changelog, to find the requester
Call startRun with nova:<key>, which joins the run if it is already open
practice.why: The accountId is needed to read the changelog, every page must be read before the list is complete, and startRun comes last because a run needs its requester from the start.

practice.q: The changelog filter keeps every hand-over to Nova. Which one names the requester?
practice.hint: The changelog is oldest first, and the most recent hand-over wins.
practice.why: at(-1) is the last element, the latest hand-over. at(0) would name whoever assigned it to Nova first, even if they took it back.

practice.q: Nova assigns RH-1234 back to Sean when the PR is ready. The next poll sees that change in the changelog. What must happen?

options.text: Treat it as Sean stopping Nova
options.why: Unassigning Nova by a person means stop, but this change was made by Nova itself.

options.text: Ignore it, because its author is Nova's own accountId
options.why: The poll never reacts to Nova's own actions; otherwise Nova would end up talking to itself.

options.text: Start a new run, because the ticket changed
options.why: A change made by Nova is not a hand-over, and the run already exists.
